transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Uh… yeah. I guess I’m here because things have just felt kind of… stuck. I’m trying not to make it sound worse than it is, but honestly, I can’t really see my studio—or my life, I guess—getting back on track anymore. No matter how hard I work, or whatever payment plan they put in front of me, it just feels like it’s not going to be enough. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed feeling down or hopeless most of the time, even when things aren’t particularly stressful?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but most days I wake up and it’s like this heavy gray feeling is already there before anything’s even happened. And even at the shop, around the wood and tools and all that stuff I used to really care about, it just feels kind of flat. Sometimes I catch myself just standing there staring, and I have to push myself to get moving. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you found yourself worrying a lot about specific things related to your studio or life situation, or avoiding certain situations because they feel overwhelming or stressful?

I’m not sure… I mean, I worry about the studio some, sure, but it feels more like it’s just there in the background than one specific thing I’m panicking over. I don’t think I’m really avoiding things because of stress, at least not on purpose. I just… sometimes don’t have much in me to deal with things. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like your work in the studio or other activities, don’t interest you as much anymore—or maybe not at all?

Yeah… I mean, I guess that’s been happening. I don’t want to make it sound like I don’t care at all, but most days I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling already sitting on me. And even when I’m in the shop, around the wood and everything I used to really love, it just… feels flat. Sometimes I have to kind of fight myself not to just stand there staring. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or that you don’t have the energy to do things you normally would do, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yeah… I mean, I do get tired. Probably more than I should. By midmorning sometimes my arms feel like I’ve already been hauling lumber all day, even if I haven’t done that much yet. I can sleep a full night and still feel like I’m dragging myself through measuring, cutting, even just returning calls.

I don’t want to sound lazy or anything… I’m still trying to get things done. It’s just like I run out of gas really early. Is that the sort of tired you mean?
Has there been a time recently when you felt no interest or pleasure in almost any activity, even the ones you used to enjoy the most?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to say there’s nothing at all, because that sounds dramatic, but most days I wake up and it’s like this heavy gray feeling is already there.

Even being in the shop, around the wood and tools—stuff I used to really love—it just feels kind of flat. Sometimes I have to push myself not to just stand there staring. So… yes, I guess that’s what you’re asking.
How long have you been feeling this way — this heavy, gray feeling and losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

It’s been… a while. I probably should’ve said that more clearly. I think it started around when I took on the mortgage for the studio—so a little over two years ago now. Maybe about two years and two months.

I kept telling myself it was just stress and I’d settle into it, but… it’s kind of stayed. Does that make sense?
Can you describe what your mood is like throughout the day — is that heavy, gray feeling something that’s pretty much with you all the time, or does it come and go?

It’s… it’s pretty much there most days, I’d say. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m never okay, but I usually wake up and that heavy, gray feeling is already sitting on me.

And even at the shop, with the wood and everything I used to really enjoy, it just feels kind of flat. Some days I have to kind of push myself not to just stand there staring. Is that… is that what you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past couple of years — like eating more or less than usual or gaining or losing weight without trying?

I don’t think so… not in any big way, at least. My eating’s maybe a little uneven sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed my weight changing without trying or anything like that.

I’m sorry, I know that’s kind of a vague answer. I just don’t think appetite or weight has been the main thing I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep — like trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual — even when there’s no clear reason for it?

I’m not really sure there’s been a clear change there. I mean, I have nights that aren’t great, but I don’t know if it’s outside the normal kind of thing, you know?

I haven’t noticed myself sleeping a lot more or anything like that. And I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Sleep hasn’t been the main thing I’ve been thinking about, if that answers it okay.
Have you experienced days where even small tasks, like getting dressed or making a phone call, felt like they took all the energy you had — even when you didn’t do much physically?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just lazy or anything, but yes, that happens.

By midmorning sometimes my arms feel like I’ve already been hauling lumber all day, even if I haven’t really done that much yet. And even after a full night in bed, I’ll be at the shop trying to measure or cut, or I’ll need to return a simple phone call, and it just feels like I’m pushing through mud. Like I can do it, usually, but it wipes me out more than it seems like it should.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you experienced days where you felt absolutely no interest or pleasure in anything, even things you used to really enjoy?

I don’t know if I’d say absolutely no interest in anything. That sounds… pretty strong, and I don’t want to overstate it.

There are times I don’t feel much pull toward things, even things I’d normally like, but I’m not sure I’d describe it as nothing at all. Sometimes I can still get some enjoyment once I’m actually doing something. It’s more like I have to push myself to get there, if that makes sense.

I’m not sure if that answers what you’re asking.
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re not good enough, or that you’re failing—even at things you used to manage easily?

Yeah… I guess I have, though I’m not proud of saying that.

Like, if a joint doesn’t line up just right, or I miss getting a bid in on time, I don’t just think, “Okay, I made a mistake.” I start going straight to, “Maybe I’m just a lousy carpenter,” or “Maybe I had no business trying to run my own studio in the first place.”

I know that probably sounds a little dramatic when I say it out loud. I do try to correct myself, but in the moment it feels pretty true. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have there been times when even things that usually make you happy, like finishing a good piece of work or seeing a project come together, don’t feel satisfying at all?

I’m not sure I’d say it doesn’t feel satisfying at all. I mean… when a piece comes together, I can usually still recognize that it’s good work, and there’s some part of me that’s glad it turned out right.

It’s just maybe not always as strong as I think it should be. Sometimes it’s more like, “Okay, that’s done,” instead of really feeling proud of it. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
